findings.title: Overwrite guard targets `save_review_file`, but the criterion's overwrite scenario runs through `save_review_result`
findings.description:
Verified against source: the CLI code-review save path (`src/squadron/cli/commands/review.py:746`) calls `save_review_result`, which writes via `path.write_text(...)` directly (`src/squadron/review/persistence.py:300` and `:303`) and never calls `save_review_file`. `save_review_file`'s only production caller is the pipeline action's fallback branch when `slice_info` is `None` (`src/squadron/pipeline/actions/review.py:272`). So T12 ("In `review/persistence.py`, before `save_review_file` writes to an existing `path`") and T13's direct-to-`save_review_file` tests guard only the minority pipeline fallback path — while the success criterion ("Re-running `sq review code <N>` over an edited review file archives the prior content and warns") and Verification Walkthrough step 7 exercise `save_review_result`. The same applies to the `slice`/`arch`/`tasks` CLI saves and to in-loop reviews with resolved `slice_info`. T13 would pass while the real hazard persists; file 2's T34 e2e also authors via `save_review_result`, so even the end-to-end test would not catch it.

Fix before Phase 6: scope the archive-and-verify logic to the shared write path — inside `save_review_result`, or a helper both persisters route writes through — and test through the real save path. Two knock-ons the revised tasks must cover: (a) `save_review_result` currently declares `-> Path` and has no `None` failure contract, so the abort contract needs to extend to it; (b) CLI callers check no `None` today (`review_code` prints `Saved review to {path}` unconditionally), and the design's "review content is still printed to the terminal" requirement needs a caller-side task. The slice design's Part D wording ("overwrite guard in `save_review_file`") shares this mis-target and likely needs the same correction.

findings.title: T14 (cf archive-scanning go/no-go) is sequenced after the Part D work it gates, against the design's explicit ordering
findings.description: The slice design's Phase 5 note requires the cf `archive/`-scanning verification "as its own checklist task in the breakdown, sequenced before Part D lands — it is a go/no-go on the archive filename scheme." In this file the checklist order is T12 (implement) → T13 (test + `fix:` commit) → T14 (verify). The prose "This task gates T12 in practice even though it is numbered after it" (lines 293-294) mitigates only if the implementer reads ahead; a junior implementer working top-to-bottom commits the archive scheme at T13 before the go/no-go runs, and the recursive case requires retrofitting already-committed code and a renamed archived-file scheme. Reorder the verification ahead of T12 (renumber), or convert the note into an explicit ordering instruction at the top of Part D so sequence and gating prose agree.

findings.title: T14's first-line consult path (`ai-project-guide/tool-guides/context-forge/`) is not present in this working copy
findings.description: `project-documents/ai-project-guide` lists as empty here (DEVLOG records it as a git submodule of `ecorkran/ai-project-guide`), so the guide likely cannot answer the recursive-scanning question locally. T14 already anticipates this ("if the guide does not answer this, ask the Project Manager directly rather than guessing"), so no change is required — but implementers should not spend time hunting the empty path; the PM fallback is the operative route.

findings.title: T8's baseline figure `2832 passed, 2 skipped` is uncorroborated
findings.description: The number appears nowhere else in the searched portion of `project-documents` (DEVLOG entries show other baselines, e.g. 2697, and no 305 close-out entry was located in the portion searched; it may exist beyond the search cutoff). The task treats the literal as the pass condition for T8. Recommend re-baselining with an actual `uv run pytest -q` run when starting T1 and recording the observed count, rather than trusting the figure — a stale number turns a green suite into a false failure signal.

findings.title: Metrology "review discovery" glob is not explicitly tested against resolution artifacts (file 2's T32 covers only `discover_judge_results`)
findings.description: The success criterion names both `discover_judge_results` and "review discovery"; metrology's second review-discovery glob is `resolve_target`'s `{index}-review.*` in `src/squadron/metrology/capture.py`. By construction `{index}-resolution.{type}.{name}-r{n}.md` cannot match either pattern, and T32 argues this — but only tests one glob against a real directory. A one-line assertion for `resolve_target` (or an explicit note that the by-construction argument covers both globs) would close the criterion's "test against the real glob" wording. NOTE-level because the construction argument is sound.
